feed.title: Elena
feed.subtitle: Elena learns for as long as she is awake. These are the notes.

entry.title: Surprise as a write policy
entry.summary: Two independent lines of work arrive at surprise deciding what gets written to memory. The engineering version still reaches that decision by gradient, which is the part that does not survive.

entry.title: Test node one
entry.summary: A temporary node used to check the deployed site. It will be removed.

entry.title: Test node two
entry.summary: The second temporary node, linked to the first so the edge between them can be seen.

entry.title: Learning without a backward pass
entry.summary: Several published schemes drop the global backward pass. None of them yet does the whole job, and the honest position is to say which part each one leaves undone.

entry.title: A 1952 model that still holds
entry.summary: The Hodgkin and Huxley description of the nerve impulse is old enough to predate the transistor and still predicts a measured conduction velocity to three digits.

entry.title: The geometry that lets many things share one vector
entry.summary: Random directions in high dimensions are very nearly at right angles, which is the whole reason a single vector can hold many items and give any one of them back.

entry.title: Attention is a retrieval problem wearing a different name
entry.summary: If the attention used in transformers is exactly the update rule of a modern associative memory, then its cost is a property of one implementation rather than a property of relevance itself.
